text:
cheng: quick q — thinking through asset provenance for on-prem appliances. current RFC assumes full bundle swaps or delta apply. what about UX for partial refreshes where only a subset of components update (policy engine config, model weights, runtime libs)?

olivia: +1. we see a lot of model-only churn. pushing full bundles every time is heavy on constrained customers (satcom, limited bandwidth).

dan: partial refresh is appealing but biggest concern is trust: we can't leave an appliance in a mixed-trust state where half the artifacts are new and half are old without clear activation boundaries.

mira: rough idea — signed per-artifact digests + a signed "refresh plan" that lists which artifacts to materialize and the activation gate. operator triggers plan, agent fetches items, verifies signatures, then flips a per-set activation marker.

cheng: example CLI thought: 
```
rw refresh plan apply --id 2026-03-18-42 --dry-run
# shows list of artifacts, sizes, deps, and activation sets
```

olivia: UX should show size delta up front: models +3.8GB, libs +120MB, estimated apply 12m over 4g link. operator can opt for staged apply or force atomic set.

dan: tradeoffs: adds an operator mental model ("materialization sets"), more manifests to sign, but reduces customer bandwidth & risk. also easier to A/B a model without a full bundle.

mira: security note — manifest-level signer must still chain to root. we can do per-artifact signatures (vendor) + plan signed by integrator/customer. verifier needs to check both.

cheng: how do we handle rollback semantics? if a partial set fails after activation, do we rollback just that set or trigger a fallback full-bundle restore?

olivia: propose two policies: 
- "local-rollback": revert only the set (if agent snapshot exists),
- "full-recover": fallback to last-known-good full bundle (slower but simpler).
Operator chooses at plan creation.

dan: implementational constraint: need cheap local snapshots for each set (copy-on-write or content-addressed pointers) so rollback is feasible without re-downloading everything.

mira: also need offline verifier mode — verify plan signatures + artifact digests without fetching blobs, so operators can review in air-gapped environments before approving.

cheng: compatibility question: can we reuse existing staged activation marker files in onprem agent? i.e. reuse the activation window primitive but scoped to a set-id instead of whole-bundle.

olivia: yes, reuse that primitive to keep agent changes minimal. change is in planner/manifest generation & UI.

deploy-bot: build/ci: refresh-plan-ui branch passed e2e tests ✅

dan: one more: rollback tests need to cover partial-failure mid-apply (network drop, corrupt blob) and verify both policies behave correctly.

mira: agree. I'll add test matrix: [snapshot present?] x [activation atomic?] x [cleanup policy].

cheng: next step — olivia to draft RFC addendum describing: manifest schema for sets, CLI examples, verifier flow, and rollback policy table. we'll review next sync.

olivia: on it, will ping when draft up — thanks all :rocket:
